text:
Bitcoin trading is consolidating near $63,600, securing a minor 1.6% daily relief bounce as markets react to potential geopolitical resolutions in the Middle East. Despite this short-term stabilization, the digital asset class faces persistent downward pressure from a prolonged outflow streak in spot ETFs, limiting significant upward price recovery. Concurrently, legislative friction remains high as industry groups press the Senate to schedule a vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, which has been stalled despite clearing the Banking Committee.

This regulatory and ETF friction coincides with a highly anticipated June 16–17 FOMC meeting, where policymakers are expected to hold the benchmark interest rate steady in the 3.50%–3.75% range. Persistent inflation data continues to reinforce the Federal Reserve’s 'higher-for-longer' interest rate posture, keeping sovereign treasury yields elevated. As the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding digital assets rises alongside traditional yields, digital asset valuations continue to demonstrate a tight performance correlation to traditional macro liquidity and credit transmission channels.
